title: Compost Thermometer Heat-Up After Turn
dataSources: Hive metrics (`flowhive:reading`), egg counter events (`eggcounter:event`), goat RFID visits (`goattag:scan`), goat watering and feed logs (`goatcare:event`), and compost readings (`compost:reading`).
app: Smallholding and backyard telemetry from Flow Hive scales, chicken coop counters, RFID goat tags, compost thermometers, and camera-driven chore logs sent to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=compost:reading
| search temp_gain_24h_c=*
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(temp_gain_24h_c) as avg_temp_gain_24h_c max(temp_gain_24h_c) as max_temp_gain_24h_c by _time pile_id
| sort - _time
description: Tracks compost heat-up after turning over time and breaks it out by pile.
value: Heat-up after turning is a practical sign that the pile still has the air and moisture it needs.
implementation: Send compost heat-up after turning events to `index=personal` with the fields used in the breakdown and review the resulting trend at 1d granularity.
visualization: Stacked time chart of compost heat-up after turning by pile.
grandmaExplanation: It reminds how compost heat-up after turning changes over time so the busy spells and quiet spells stand out.
